title: Optimize NCCL overlap (collectives) and TP kernels + KV cache/continuous batching improvements
author: Ava Thompson
description: Motivation: In multi-GPU tensor-parallel training/inference paths we observed suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and GPU kernel execution, and inefficiencies in KV cache eviction and continuous batching that increased tail latency under bursty traffic. This PR improves NCCL stream scheduling and collective launching order, tunes stream priorities for TP collectives, refactors the TP kernel launch sequence to enable earlier compute overlap, improves KV cache hotset heuristics, and tightens the continuous batcher synchronization to reduce unnecessary kernel serialization. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a dedicated NCCL comm stream pool for TP collectives and set explicit CUDA stream priorities to ensure collectives are launched on a lower-priority stream that can overlap with compute. 2) Reorder collective vs kernel launches in nccl_scheduler to post non-blocking collectives earlier and use streamEvents to avoid unnecessary syncs. 3) Add a kernel batching fence optimization in tp_kernels to allow independent layer kernels to progress while collectives are outstanding. 4) KV cache: improve hotset tracking and prefetch/retain policy to reduce cold-fetches during continuous batching. 5) Continuous batcher: reduce cross-stream synchronization points and add an adaptive wait backoff to lower tail latency under light loads. Performance: On internal perf lab with 4x A100s and mlm-large workload we measured average per-token latency improvement of ~12% and 95th percentile improvement of ~18% with negligible loss in throughput; KV-cache hit-rate improved from 87% to 93% on a realistic prompt distribution; CPU-side scheduling overhead reduced by ~9%. Testing: Unit tests for nccl_scheduler and tp_kernels; end-to-end perf harness runs (tp_overlap_bench) across small/medium/large batch sizes; KV cache regression tests and additional flakiness fixes for continuous_batcher. Rollback plan: revert the head branch and redeploy scheduler config flag to use previous stream behavior. Related: addresses ENG-1983 and SUP-4321. Release notes: include in 0.35.1 perf section.
